answer: The haven multiplier is published, charged in walnut, and opal lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 4 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 4849 identities would post 3909 proofs and burn roughly 79 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
